Q189.reason: The conviction already established the adjudicative facts, so no further trial-type hearing is needed; full faith and credit (Art. IV) governs judgments from other states, not this board's own revocation.

Q190.reason: An involuntary confession violates due process and is inadmissible, while voluntary, non-custodial, or non-interrogation statements are not barred by those rules.

Q191.reason: Ted consented to being held out as a partner, so he is liable by estoppel and partners are jointly liable on contract debts; a lender taking only interest is not a de facto partner.
